children: OTTAWA--Canada's official international reserves decreased by $2.12 billion last month, driven by losses on reserves management operations and a net loss on investments, the federal finance department said Monday.
The country's reserves of foreign currencies and other monetary assets totaled $125.29 billion as of Sept. 29, following a $368 million increase during August to $127.41 billion.
The government reported no intervention in the foreign-currency market, and there were no gold holdings at the end of the month.
All reserve figures are reported in U.S. dollars.

The finance department said that the amount of Canada bills outstanding rose by $98 million to $1.62 billion as of the end of September. Canada bills are short-term securities sold on the U.S. money market.

At Sept. 29, foreign-currency reserves included securities of $85.72 billion, deposits of $9.5 billion, special drawing rights of $23.74 billion, and a reserve position in the International Monetary Fund of $4.11 billion, the finance department said.
